summary: Hourly metering-offset from transient test keys causing missing reserved-credit adjustment on monthly invoice
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that a line on their most recent monthly invoice shows a missing reserved-credit allocation for a ~3-hour window on 2026-02-27 01:00-04:00 UTC. The invoice shows an overage charge where they expected the dedicated reserved-rate credit to have applied.

Impact: ScribeFlow is disputing ~$2,760 in overage charges on the March invoice. This affects their finance reconciliation and they are requesting an interim provisional credit while we investigate. No immediate service degradation reported — this is a billing/usage reconciliation issue.

Environment: Dedicated (reserved pool) in prod-us-east. Customer runs an internal nightly smoke-suite from a short-lived test key during on-call drills (ephemeral test keys rotated every hour).

Steps to reproduce / observed behavior:
1) Customer ran repeated ephemeral health checks from a short-lived key between 01:10 and 03:45 UTC on 2026-02-27.
2) Metering shows these calls as normal usage in the raw postbacks.
3) The hourly accumulator run marked the window as eligible for reserved-credit smoothing, but the subsequent postback reconciler later classified many of those postbacks as "ephemeral-probe" (non-billable) and removed them from final usage.
4) Reserved credits that had been applied during the accumulator run were not re-applied after reconciliation, leaving a net overage on the published invoice.

Logs / evidence provided by customer: Customer attached export of request IDs and timestamps (included in attachments). They noted the requests carried header X-Test-Key: scribe-ephemeral-20260227-01 and showed successful 200s.

Requested outcome: Reconcile usage for the window, re-apply reserved credits if appropriate, and issue a provisional credit while the root cause is investigated. Customer also requests guidance on recommended detection/labeling for ephemeral keys so future smoke tests don't affect billing.

investigation_notes: Pulled hourly_accumulator snapshots for 2026-02-27 00:00-06:00 UTC (S3 path s3://metering-snapshots/2026-02-27/). Snapshots show reserved_credit_applied: true for windows 01:00 and 02:00 UTC.

Postback-reconciler later ran classification that moved ~83% of the ephemeral key events to classification 'probe'. The reconciler has a two-phase flow: classify -> reflow. The reflow worker hit a rate-limiter timeout (logged as "ReflowWorker.Timeout: exceeded retries") and aborted without marking the window reconciled.

Root cause hypothesis: non-idempotent order of operations between accumulator and reconciler combined with a transient rate-limiter failure prevented a credit re-apply job from running. The repro is intermittent and tied to bursty ephemeral traffic namespaced under short-lived keys.

Reproducer notes: Simulated ephemeral key burst locally and forced reconciler rate-limiter to trip; observed accumulator applying credits then reconciler classification removing usage without triggering reflow commit.
resolution: 2026-03-14 12:30 - Temporary mitigation: Issued provisional credit of $2,760 to ScribeFlow's account (internal credit memo CM-2026-03-14-SF) while engineering deploys a fix. Customer notified and accepted provisional credit.

Engineering fix: Backport PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/1289 to release branch — adds retry/backoff in reconciler reflow worker and changes order to ensure reflow is scheduled synchronously when accumulator marks a window as eligible. Deployed to prod-us-east 2026-03-14 17:05 UTC.

Post-deploy verification: Re-ran reconciliation for 2026-02-27 window in replay mode; final usage now matches expected smoothing behavior and reserved credits are re-applied. Generated reconciliation report and attached to ticket (report id: recon-2026-03-14-876543).

Follow-ups / action items:
- FIN: Convert provisional credit CM-2026-03-14-SF to permanent refund if post-deploy verification remains green after 48h.
- SRE/Infra: Monitor reflow worker error rate for 7 days; alert if >1% failure rate.
- DX/Docs: Add recommended header naming convention and detection patterns for ephemeral/test keys to public billing FAQ.
- Product: Consider adding a leash that prevents ephemeral keys from triggering reserved-credit smoothing (ticket INT-3380 for product review).
